title: Rochester-Mantorville ghost tours spark community around the strange
excerpt: For those looking to get into the Halloween spirit, Southeast Minnesota’s foremost paranormal investigator, Dr. Hawk Horvath’s local ghost tours and ghost hunting classes foster community around these collective experiences.
content:
ROCHESTER, Minn. (KTTC) – For those looking to get into the Halloween spirit, Southeast Minnesota’s foremost paranormal investigator, Dr. Hawk Horvath’s local ghost tours and ghost hunting classes foster community around these collective experiences.

Horvath has been a ghost hunter for 20 years, first inspired to try out the field after learning about the paranormal investigations of the Ohio State Prison when she was living in Pennsylvania. Horvath grabbed the last spot available to join 99 other ghost hunters in an open investigation of the prison. Upon returning to Rochester, she began her own investigative team.

Horvath’s ghost tours of the Rochester and Mantorville area, known as Hauntings with Hawk, incorporate both local history and ghost stories. Some of the sites on her tours are ones Horvath and her team, After Hours Paranormal Investigations, have personally investigated themselves. Among these locations are the Rochester Civic and Repertory Theatres, Rochester State Hospital, and Mantorville Opera House.

While the team uses typical ghost hunting equipment such as infrared cameras and digital voice recorders, Horvath said their approach in searching for ghosts is unique.

“My team does not believe in provoking,” Horvath explained. “We never provoke. We are kind. We are gentle. We are respectful. We use our pleases and our thank yous. And. you know, surprisingly, this is not what it looks like on TV.”

Horvath also teaches a regular series of adult classes through Rochester Public Schools Community Education about ghost hunting. The courses culminate in a hands-on ghost investigation that students are able to participate in. Her most recent class had 34 students.

“All adults who are just so excited to want to learn more about it,” Horvath said. “I think because nobody talks about it.”

One of the reasons people are interested in the supernatural, Horvath believes, is out of a desire to explain their own unexplainable experiences.

“I always look at a class and say, ‘you know, you look pretty normal, but you know this is ghost hunting. This is not basket weaving or intermediate crochet,’” Horvath continued. “And they all just beam because they have their own experiences and they just want it normalized. They want to know it’s okay. So, I like to provide a safe place for people.”

Dr. Horvath’s upcoming second book, Into the Deep, will contain similar stories of her experience as a ghost hunter, psychic, and medium.

You can book a spot for a Hauntings with Hawk tour on her website.
